explanations.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, says the opposite here. His example says “…the sign or wonder he has spoken to you comes about…” So this prophet's sign really happens. That's what makes the example so sneaky.

Right, baker. In Moses' example the sign or wonder does come about, but the prophet says “Let us follow other gods…” So he gets his prediction right and still points Israel away from the LORD. A good track record is nice, but it's not the whole picture.

explanations.answer: Follow other gods and worship them
explanations.explanation: That's what Moses says. The prophet says “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them…” That's the invitation, to follow and worship gods Israel has not known. It's a big ask, and the sign coming about doesn't change what he's asking.
Moses doesn't say that. He never has the prophet ask to lead anybody. What the prophet says is “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them…”

explanations.answer: Build an altar on every hill
explanations.explanation: No altars come up in this verse, friend. An altar on every hill? That's a lot of hills and a lot of stone hauling, and nobody in the verse signs up for that job. What the prophet asks is “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them…” His ask is about following and worshiping.

That's it. Moses says “…you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer.” The sign came true, but the message still pulls away from the LORD. Israel isn't told to be impressed. They're told not to listen.

Moses doesn't offer a second sign, baker. The instruction is “…you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer.” Waiting around for more proof isn't part of it. The reason Moses gives is “For the LORD your God is testing you to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.”
Priests don't come up in this verse. Moses gives the answer himself: “…you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer.” The verse leaves no room for a vote.

Yes, baker. Moses says “…the LORD your God is testing you to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” So a prophet with a true sign shows up as a test of Israel's love. That's the word Moses picks.
Close, but that's not the word Moses uses. He says the LORD is testing them, “…to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” It's about what's in their hearts.
Moses doesn't say punishing. He says “…the LORD your God is testing you…” The test is to find out whether they love Him with all their heart and all their soul.

That one's on the list. Moses says “serve Him and hold fast to Him.” He gives six things in all, and holding fast sits right at the end. It's like holding onto a hot tray with oven mitts. Nobody lets go halfway.

Nope, no temple on this one, friend. Moses is talking about how Israel lives, not what they build. He says “You are to follow the LORD your God and fear Him.” Then he adds “Keep His commandments and listen to His voice; serve Him and hold fast to Him.” Every item there is something Israel does, not something they construct.
Daily gifts aren't on this list, friend. Moses says “Keep His commandments and listen to His voice; serve Him and hold fast to Him.” The list is about following and holding on to Him.

explanations.answer: He urged them to rebel against the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says the prophet “…has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God…” He also says the prophet tried to turn them from the way the LORD commanded them to walk. That's the reason Moses gives.

explanations.answer: He lied about the sign he gave
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. In Moses' example the sign actually comes about. The reason he gives is that the prophet “…has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God…”

explanations.answer: He claimed to be Israel's king
explanations.explanation: Kings don't come into this verse at all. Moses' reason is that the prophet “…has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God…” It's about turning them away from the LORD.

That's true, baker. Moses calls Him the LORD “…who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery…” So the rebellion is against the One who already rescued them. That's the weight behind the whole warning.
It's true, actually. Moses says the LORD “…brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery…” That's who the prophet would be turning them away from.

explanations.answer: Their own family or closest friend
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Moses names “…your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend…” These are the people closest to you. I think that's why this part is so heavy.

explanations.answer: A traveler from a far land
explanations.explanation: Moses does mention far-off places, but only for the gods. He says they're the gods “…of the peoples around you, whether near or far…” The one doing the enticing is “…your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend…”

explanations.answer: A priest serving at the altar
explanations.explanation: No priest is named here. Moses pictures “…your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend…” It's someone close to home.

True. Moses says this person “…secretly entices you…” The word is secretly, so it's a private pitch. And it comes from someone close: a brother, a son or daughter, the wife you embrace, or a closest friend.

The text says it's true, baker. Moses says this person “…secretly entices you…” The pitch is to go and worship other gods. So the pull happens in secret, not out in the open. And it comes from someone close: a brother, a son or daughter, the wife you embrace, or a closest friend.

Moses says the opposite. His words are “Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.” I think this one is heavy, since the person is family or a close friend. Moses gives the reason that this person tried to turn them away from the LORD their God.

Right, baker. Moses says “Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.” I think this one is heavy, because it's someone close. The text names a brother, a son or daughter, a wife and a closest friend.

explanations.answer: He tried to turn them from the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says to stone him “…for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” The reason is about turning them from the LORD. It's the same reason he gave for the prophet.

explanations.answer: He broke a promise to his family
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. Moses gives one reason: “…for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God…” Promises to family aren't mentioned.

Stealing isn't in the verse, friend. Moses says to stone him “…for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” That's the whole reason.

Yes, baker. Moses says “…all Israel will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such a wicked thing among you.” So the news reaches all Israel, everyone. They hear it, they're afraid, and Moses says they will never again do such a wicked thing among them.
Close, but not the word. Moses says all Israel “…will hear and be afraid…” Anger isn't in the verse.
Proud doesn't fit this one. Moses says all Israel “…will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such a wicked thing among you.” The word is afraid.
That's what Moses says. His words are “…you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly.” A report is only a report until it's checked. That's three verbs in a row, so he really means it.
That's not what Moses says. First comes the checking: “…you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly.” Nobody marches anywhere on a rumor.

explanations.answer: Send a prophet to warn it
explanations.explanation: A prophet isn't mentioned here. Moses says to “…inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly.” The first job is finding out what's true.
The text says otherwise. Moses says to act only “…if it is established with certainty that this abomination has been committed among you…” The checking has to come first. A report alone isn't enough.
Right, baker. Moses says the action comes only “…if it is established with certainty…” That's why he says to inquire, investigate and interrogate thoroughly. Certainty comes first.

explanations.answer: Burn it along with the city
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says to “…completely burn the city and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God.” The plunder doesn't go home with anyone. It goes into the fire with the city.
Moses doesn't say that. After the plunder is gathered in the public square, he says to “…completely burn the city and all its plunder…” Nothing gets divided up.

Priests don't show up in this verse, friend. Nobody gets a cut here, not even the priests. Moses says the city and everything taken from it goes up “…as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God.” Whole means whole, so there's no leftover pile to hand out.
Moses says the opposite. He says “The city must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.” There's no someday in that sentence. It stays a ruin.
Right, baker. Moses says “The city must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.” That's a heavy picture, with no someday in it. The word is forever.
Yes. Moses says that when nothing devoted clings to their hands, “…the LORD will turn from His fierce anger…” So Israel holding nothing back changes how this ends. That's right in the verse.
Famine isn't what Moses names here. He says “…the LORD will turn from His fierce anger…” That's the thing the LORD turns from.
Exile isn't in this verse, friend. Moses says “…the LORD will turn from His fierce anger…” That's what he says the LORD turns from.

Yes, that's on the list. Moses says the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” Mercy, compassion and growing numbers are all there. I'd say that's a lot of good news after a hard stretch.
A king isn't on Moses' list in this verse. He says the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” Those are the three things named.
Rain isn't mentioned here, friend. Moses says the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” That's the whole list.

True, baker. Moses says this is “…because you obey the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments I am giving you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.” The verse before it names the mercy: the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” Those reasons are spelled out in the verse itself.

The text says it's true. Moses says all of this comes “…because you obey the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments I am giving you today…” He adds “…doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.”
